relevance_reason: Reports de novo RRAGC missense variants in 3 infants with a fatal early-onset mTORopathy (cardiomyopathy, hepatopathy, brain malformations), with functional studies; this establishes the disorder.

findings.statement: Reijnders et al. (2023) reported 3 infants with dilated cardiomyopathy, hepatopathy, and brain abnormalities, including pachygyria, polymicrogyria, and septo-optic dysplasia. The authors described the disorder as an early-onset mTORopathy with an unfavorable prognosis.
quotes: 3 infants with dilated cardiomyopathy, hepatopathy, and brain abnormalities, including pachygyria, polymicrogyria, and septo-optic dysplasia
cause of an early-onset mTORopathy with unfavorable prognosis

findings.statement: In an infant with this disorder, Reijnders et al. (2023) used trio exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous missense variant in the RRAGC gene, c.269C>A (p.Thr90Asn). This variant had previously been reported as a somatic variant in follicular lymphoma. Patient fibroblasts carrying the variant showed increased cell size, dysregulated p70S6K and TFEB signaling, and mTOR subcellular localization that was decoupled from metabolic state. The authors concluded that these findings were in line with constitutive overactivation of mTORC1.
quotes: We identified 3 de novo missense variants in RRAGC (NM_022157.4: c.269C>A, p.(Thr90Asn), c.353C>T, p.(Pro118Leu), and c.343T>C, p.(Trp115Arg)), which were previously reported as occurring somatically in follicular lymphoma.

Studies of patient-derived fibroblasts carrying the p.(Thr90Asn) variant revealed increased cell size, as well as dysregulation of mTOR-related p70S6K (ribosomal protein S6 kinase 1) and transcription factor EB signaling.
Moreover, subcellular localization of mTOR was decoupled from metabolic state.

findings.statement: In an infant with this disorder, Reijnders et al. (2023) identified a de novo heterozygous missense variant in the RRAGC gene, c.353C>T (p.Pro118Leu), by trio exome sequencing. The variant had previously been reported as a somatic variant in follicular lymphoma, and the key cellular findings were confirmed in a HEK293 cell model.
quotes: We identified 3 de novo missense variants in RRAGC (NM_022157.4: c.269C>A, p.(Thr90Asn), c.353C>T, p.(Pro118Leu), and c.343T>C, p.(Trp115Arg)), which were previously reported as occurring somatically in follicular lymphoma.
We confirmed the key findings for all RRAGC variants described in this study in a HEK293 cell model.

findings.statement: In an infant with this disorder, Reijnders et al. (2023) identified a de novo heterozygous missense variant in the RRAGC gene, c.343T>C (p.Trp115Arg), by trio exome sequencing. The variant had previously been reported as a somatic variant in follicular lymphoma, and the key cellular findings were confirmed in a HEK293 cell model.
quotes: We identified 3 de novo missense variants in RRAGC (NM_022157.4: c.269C>A, p.(Thr90Asn), c.353C>T, p.(Pro118Leu), and c.343T>C, p.(Trp115Arg)), which were previously reported as occurring somatically in follicular lymphoma.
We confirmed the key findings for all RRAGC variants described in this study in a HEK293 cell model.

findings.statement: Reijnders et al. (2023) concluded that the cellular findings for all 3 RRAGC variants were in line with constitutive overactivation of the mTORC1 pathway. They showed this in patient fibroblasts and confirmed it in HEK293 cells.
quotes: The above results are in line with a constitutive overactivation of the mTORC1 pathway.
We confirmed the key findings for all RRAGC variants described in this study in a HEK293 cell model.

relevance_reason: The paper provides the functional and animal-model evidence establishing pathogenicity of the de novo RRAGC S75Y variant identified in a pediatric syndromic dilated cardiomyopathy patient, the gene/variant underlying this entry, plus mechanism and candidate therapy.

findings.statement: Kim et al. (2021) noted that whole exome sequencing of a pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) patient had previously identified a de novo S75Y variant in Rag GTPase protein C (RagC, RRAGC), revealing RRAGC as a new susceptibility gene, and stated that further evidence including functional studies in animal models was required to prove pathogenicity.
quotes: Through whole exome sequencing of a pediatric DCM patient, we recently identified a de novo S75Y variant in Rag GTPase protein C (RagC, or RRAGC), revealing RRAGC as a new susceptibility gene. However, further evidence is required to prove pathogenicity, including functional studies in animal models and identification of additional RRAGC mutations in DCM cohorts.

A de novo missense variant in Rag GTPase protein C (RagCS75Y) was recently identified in a syndromic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) patient. However, its pathogenicity and the related therapeutic strategy remain unclear.

findings.statement: Kim et al. (2021) reviewed that the S75 residue of RagC is evolutionarily conserved from yeast to human and lies in the phosphate-binding loop (P-loop) motif mediating GTP/GDP binding, that recurrent somatic RRAGC S75 mutations (S75C, S75N, S75F) occur in follicular lymphoma with greater GDP-binding affinity and hyperactive mTORC1 signaling, and that in silico protein modeling predicted S75Y also increases the GDP-bound state, supporting a gain-of-function mechanism.
quotes: The S75 site in RagC is evolutionarily conserved from yeast to human beings, and is located in the phosphate-binding loop (P-loop) motif that is known to mediate GTP/GDP binding. Many cases of RRAGC S75 mutation, including S75C, S75N, S75F, were identified from follicular lymphoma patients.

Based on in silico protein modeling via computational structural analysis, it is predicted that the S75Y mutation increases the GDP-bound state, leading to the hypothesis that S75Y is also a gain-of-function (GOF) mutation.

findings.statement: Kim et al. (2021) generated a zebrafish rragca S56Y knock-in line (corresponding to human RagC S75Y) by TALEN-mediated editing, introducing a C-to-A conversion confirmed by Sanger sequencing and tracked by a newly created RsaI site; homozygous rragc KI fish had unchanged rragca mRNA levels in adult hearts.
quotes: we targeted the rragca locus and generated a S56Y KI zebrafish via transcription activator-like effectors nucleases (TALEN) technology. A conversion of C to A was introduced, resulting in a substitution of Serine (S) by Tyrosine (Y) at amino acid 56, corresponding to the S75Y mutation in human RagC (Figure 1A).
We obtained RragcS56Y homozygous mutants, termed rragc KI for simplicity. We noted unchanged rragca mRNA levels in adult rragc KI hearts by RT-qPCR (Figure 1D).

findings.statement: Kim et al. (2021) found that rragc S56Y knock-in zebrafish began to die at 5 months with about 70% surviving to 1 year, had reduced body weight and reduced maximum swimming capacity, and showed ventricular systolic dysfunction with reduced ejection fraction and fractional shortening, increased end-systolic volume/body weight ratio, decreased E/A ratio, increased myocardial performance index, enlarged ventricular surface area/body weight, reduced trabecular density, and elevated ventricular myosin heavy chain (vmhc) transcript, which the authors concluded confirmed pathogenicity of the S75Y variant.
quotes: The rragc KI fish started to die at 5 months, with approximately 70% fish surviving to 1 year of age (Figure 1E).

The rragc KI fish exhibited impaired growth as indicated by lower body weight (Figure 1F). Maximum swimming capacity, a heart failure index that mimics exercise capacity in humans, was significantly reduced in the rragc KI mutants (Figure 1G). We noted significant ventricular systolic function decline, a hallmark of cardiomyopathy, by measuring ejection fraction (EF) and fractional shortening (FS)

The isolated rragc KI hearts had enlarged ventricular surface area (VSA)/BW and reduced density of ventricular trabeculae (Figure 2C). We also assessed transcriptional changes of molecular markers of cardiac remodeling and detected significant elevation of ventricular myosin heavy chain (vmhc) (Figure 2D). These data confirmed pathogenicity of the S75Y variant.

phenotypes.text: growth impairment with low body weight

findings.statement: Kim et al. (2021) obtained two rragca knockout alleles as byproducts of the knock-in approach (a 124-bp insertion in exon 1 causing a premature stop codon with 60% reduction of rragca transcripts, and a 10-nucleotide deletion also predicted to truncate the protein); homozygotes for either allele showed no noticeable phenotype up to at least 1 year of age and preserved cardiac pump function, demonstrating that knock-in but not knockout recapitulated cardiomyopathy and supporting a gain-of-function mechanism.
quotes: M1 allele contains a 124 bp addition in exon1 that results in a premature stop codon and a 60% reduction of the rragca transcripts, while M2 allele contains a 10-nucleotide deletion that is also predicted to result in a premature stop codon (Figure S3A,B). Homozygous mutants for either allele did not exhibit any noticeable phenotypes until at least 1 year of age (data not shown).
These in vivo data demonstrated that rragc KI, but not rragca KO, recapitulated phenotypic features of cardiomyopathy as observed in the human patient with RagCS75Y.

findings.statement: Kim et al. (2021) showed that adenoviral overexpression of RagCS75Y, but not wild-type RagC, increased neonatal rat ventricular cardiomyocyte size 1.5-fold and raised hypertrophic markers Nppa, Nppb and Mhc7 with downregulation of Mhc6, indicating that the pathogenicity of the S75Y variant is conserved and recapitulated in vitro.
quotes: We found that overexpression of RagCS75Y via adenovirus infection for 48 h significantly increased the cell size (by 1.5 fold) when compared to control cells infected with Ad:GFP. By contrast, overexpression of wild type RagC did not affect cell size (Figure 3A–C).

Consistently, mRNA expression levels of hypertrophic markers such as Nppa, Nppb, and Mhc7 were elevated in RagCS75Y cells, whereas the expression of Mhc6 was downregulated (Figure 3D). Thus, we concluded that the pathogenicity of the S75Y variant can be recapitulated in the in vitro system.

findings.statement: Kim et al. (2021) found that RagCS75Y-expressing cardiomyocytes had hyperactive mTORC1 signaling (increased P-p70S6K and P-S6), reduced TFEB with a higher-molecular-weight band retained in the cytoplasmic rather than nuclear fraction, reduced TFEB target gene expression, blunted LC3-II induction by fasting or bafilomycin-A1, accumulation of ubiquitin-conjugated proteins in the insoluble fraction and more aggresomes, indicating insufficient autophagy flux.
quotes: we found hyperactive mTORC1 signaling as indicated by significantly higher phosphorylation levels of p70S6 kinase (P-p70S6K) and ribosomal protein S6 (P-S6) in S75Y-overexpressed NRVCMs when compared to GFP-infected control cells (Figure 4A,B). In contrast, TFEB expression was reduced and accompanied by an extra band with higher molecular weight

We then revealed that the majority of TFEB in GFP- or RagCWT transfected cells was in the nuclear fractions (lower band), while majority of TFEB in RagCS75Y transfected cells was in the cytoplasm (upper band in Figure 4C).

Fasting or Bafilomycin-A1 (BafA1) treatment significantly induced LC3-II levels in control cells but not in S75Y cardiomyocytes (Figure 4E), suggesting insufficient autophagy response and flux. Consistently, we noted accumulation of ubiquitin-conjugated proteins in the S75Y cell lysates

findings.statement: Kim et al. (2021) showed that rragc S56Y knock-in zebrafish hearts recapitulated the cellular findings, with downregulated TFEB-controlled lysosomal genes, severely reduced LC3-II unresponsive to bafilomycin-A1, elevated ubiquitin-conjugated proteins, and significantly increased glycogen deposits on Periodic Acid-Schiff staining at 1 year of age; the authors concluded that RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy is characterized by dysregulated autophagy-lysosomal clearance and glycogen deposition with both mTORC1 activation and TFEB inhibition.
quotes: transcript levels of several TFEB-controlled lysosome genes were downregulated in the rragc KI fish hearts (Figure 5A), suggesting a reduced TFEB activity. We also detected autophagy dysregulation, as indicated by LC3-II protein levels being severely reduced at steady state and unresponsive to BafA1 administration (Figure 5B).

we performed Periodic Acid–Schiff staining and observed a significant increase of glycogen deposits in rragc KI fish heart at 1 year of age (Figure 5D). Collectively, our data indicated that the RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy is characterized with dysregulated autophagy–lysosomal clearance and glycogen deposition. At the molecular level, the primary signaling defect consists of both mTORC1 activation and TFEB inhibition.

findings.statement: Kim et al. (2021) found that although TFEB phosphorylation at the mTORC1 site S211 was increased in RagCS75Y cells and was attenuated by rapamycin, rapamycin did not promote TFEB nuclear translocation; co-immunoprecipitation in AD293 cells revealed greater binding between RagCS75Y and TFEB than between RagCWT and TFEB that was not reduced by rapamycin, leading the authors to propose that mTOR-independent binding of RagCS75Y to TFEB restricts TFEB nuclear translocation and is the key pathological event leading to cardiomyopathy.
quotes: In cells containing RagCS75Y, TFEB phosphorylation at S211, an mTORC1 phosphorylation site, was significantly increased, and can be effectively attenuated by rapamycin (Figure 6G), suggesting a normal mTOR–TFEB phosphorylation signaling. However, rapamycin treatment did not translocate more TFEB into nuclei (Figure 6H)

Co-immunoprecipitation assay in AD293 cells revealed a greater binding affinity between RagCS75Y and TFEB than RagCWT and TFEB (Figure 6I). Importantly, rapamycin did not attenuate Rags–TFEB interaction, nor did promote TFEB nuclear translocation (Figure 6H,I).

we uncovered that the S75Y substitution significantly increases the binding between Rags and TFEB, and subsequently affects the nuclear translocation of TFEB. This is likely a key pathological event that ultimately leads to cardiomyopathy.

findings.statement: Kim et al. (2021) reported that mTOR inhibition was ineffective against RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy: 24-hour rapamycin or torin treatment failed to normalize enlarged RagCS75Y cardiomyocyte size despite drastic suppression of mTORC1 activity, and mtor haploinsufficiency in rragc KI;mtor+/- double mutant zebrafish failed to improve cardiac pump dysfunction, vmhc marker expression, growth, or survival.
quotes: we found 24-hour treatment with mTOR inhibitors, including rapamycin and torin, failed to normalize the enlarged cell size in S75Y NRVCMs, despite drastic inhibition of mTORC1 activity as indicated by P-S6 expression (Figure 6A–C and Figure S4A).

Similarly, haploinsufficiency of mtor failed to exert therapeutic effect on the rragc KI model, as indicated by persistent cardiac pump dysfunction, unchanged cardiomyopathy marker expression, impaired growth, and reduced survival in double mutants (Figure 6D–F and Figure S4B).

findings.statement: Kim et al. (2021) showed that TFEB activation ameliorated RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy: ectopic TFEB expression normalized the enlarged cardiomyocyte size, and a cardiomyocyte-specific Tg(cmlc2:tfeb-GFP) transgene expressing tfeb 9-fold above wild type restored ejection fraction, fractional shortening and vmhc expression and significantly improved survival in rragc KI fish, with exogenous TFEB detected in nuclei and restoration of autophagy flux, leading the authors to conclude that TFEB activation, but not mTOR inhibition, is therapeutic.
quotes: ectopic expression of TFEB was able to normalize NRVCM size that was enlarged by RagCS75Y (Figure 7A,B and Figure S5A). Next, we generated Tg(cmlc2:tfeb-GFP), a transgenic fish line that drives cardiomyocyte-specific tfeb expression 9-fold higher than wild type control (Figure 7C).

the transgene was sufficient to attenuate cardiomyopathy phenotypes in the rragc KI model, as indicated by restoration of EF, FS, and vmhc expression in rragc KI;Tg(tfeb) fish compared to age matched rragc KI alone at 7 months (Figure 7D,E). The overall survival of rragc KI;Tg(tfeb) fish was significantly improved compared to rragc KI mutants
In summary, we concluded that TFEB activation, but not mTOR inhibition, is therapeutic to RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy.

findings.statement: Kim et al. (2021) concluded from combined in vivo and in vitro evidence that S75Y is a pathogenic gain-of-function mutation in RagC that leads to cardiomyopathy, with defective mTOR-TFEB signaling as a primary pathological step, and noted that it remains to be determined whether follicular lymphoma occurs in RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy patients.
quotes: These findings suggest that S75Y is a pathogenic gain-of-function mutation in RagC that leads to cardiomyopathy. A primary pathological step of RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy is defective mTOR-TFEB signaling, which can be corrected by TFEB overexpression, but not mTOR inhibition.

It remains to be determined whether follicular lymphoma occurs in RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy patients, and if so, whether and why cardiomyocytes and lymphocytes are more susceptible than the other organs to pathological damages incurred by RagC GOF.

relevance_reason: This is the first report of a patient with syndromic fetal dilated cardiomyopathy caused by a de novo RRAGC mutation, with functional studies. It directly establishes LNGODS.

findings.statement: Long et al. (2016) reported a girl of white European ancestry who was diagnosed with fetal cardiomegaly at 30 weeks' gestation and was delivered 1 week later because of fetal hydrops. After birth, echocardiography showed severe enlargement of both ventricles and both atria, severe systolic dysfunction (LVEF 25%), a small apical ventricular septal defect, and a moderate secundum atrial septal defect. She also had bilateral cataracts and mild facial dysmorphism: wide-set eyes, downslanting palpebral fissures, prominent forehead, mild macrocephaly, and low-set ears. Extensive metabolic and genetic testing did not find a cause, and echocardiograms showed that her parents did not have asymptomatic DCM.
quotes: A 22-month-old female of white European ancestry was diagnosed with fetal cardiomegaly at 30 weeks gestation and delivered one week later for fetal hydrops.

Postnatal echocardiography revealed severe biventricular and biatrial chamber enlargement, severe systolic dysfunction (left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) 25%; normal >50%), a small apical ventricular septal defect, and a moderate secundum atrial septal defect.
Mild facial dysmorphism (wide-set eyes, down-slanted palpebral fissures, prominent forehead, mild macrocephaly, low-set ears) and bilateral cataracts were also identified.

findings.statement: Long et al. (2016) reported that the patient needed 2 months in hospital for prematurity and heart failure, and her systolic function improved on medical therapy. At 4 months of age she received a gastrostomy tube for oral aversion and failure to thrive. Her cardiac function then declined gradually, and at 21 months she was admitted twice for decompensated heart failure (LVEF 22%) with restrictive physiology. During these admissions she had transient hypoglycemia, elevated lactate, and very high transaminases, which the authors attributed to low cardiac output and congestive hepatopathy. Skin and muscle biopsies showed no respiratory chain or mitochondrial DNA abnormalities. She died at 22 months of age of multisystem organ failure due to end-stage heart failure.
quotes: At four months of age, a gastrostomy tube was placed for oral aversion and failure to thrive.

The patient suffered a gradual decline in cardiac function, necessitating two hospital admissions at 21 months of age for decompensated heart failure (LVEF 22%) with severe biatrial enlargement indicative of restrictive physiology.
died shortly thereafter at 22 months of age with intractable multisystem organ failure due to severe, end-stage heart failure.

phenotypes.text: death in early childhood from heart failure

findings.statement: Clinical exome sequencing of the patient alone found no cause. Long et al. (2016) then performed trio-based whole-exome sequencing and identified a de novo heterozygous c.224C>A (NM_022157.3) mutation in RRAGC, resulting in a ser75-to-tyr (S75Y) substitution in the highly conserved P-loop of the GTPase domain. Sanger sequencing confirmed the mutation. SIFT and PolyPhen2 predicted it to be damaging, and it was absent from ExAC. ExAC controls had no missense or truncating variants in the RRAGC GTPase domain. In silico modeling predicted that the mutation would disrupt Mg(2+) and ligand coordination and cause conformational expansion of the GDP-bound state.
quotes: the resultant c.224C>A, p.S75Y (NM_022157.3) substitution in RRAGC, predicted damaging by SIFT and PolyPhen2, remained as the single most plausible candidate.
The de novo missense mutation occurred in the highly conserved GTPase binding-domain (Figure 1D) and was absent in the ExAc database.
MD trajectories were summarized using RMSD and revealed consistent conformational expansion of the GDP-bound state for both S75Y and S75L (Figure 2G-H).

findings.statement: Long et al. (2016) overexpressed RagC(S75Y) in AD293 cells. Compared with wildtype RagC, the mutant partly prevented the loss of S6K and S6 phosphorylation during amino acid starvation, showing increased mTORC1 signaling. The authors concluded that the mutation is gain-of-function and activates mTORC1.
quotes: By contrast, S6K and S6 phosphorylation levels were increased in cells transfected with RagCS75Y (Figure 3A, B), indicating that the S75Y mutation rendered cells partially insensitive to amino acid deprivation and resulted in activated mTORC1 signaling.
